title: The Weird Brain Hack Hiding in Every Single Meal You Eat
seoTitle: Chewing and Brain Health: The Hack in Every Meal
description: Chewing more boosts blood flow to the brain, wakes up its focus centers, and calms the mind. Learn the 30-chew habit and how to start today.
author: Lori King, MD
excerpt: It's not a supplement, a superfood, or a new habit - it's something you already do at every meal. You just need to do it better. The science on chewing and brain activation is more surprising than it sounds.

title: The 5-Minute Brain Workout Hiding Inside Gym Class
description: Cross-lateral movement strengthens the bridge between your brain hemispheres, sharpening memory, focus, and balance. Try these 3 moves in 5–7 minutes.
author: Lori King, MD
excerpt: Zulu dancers, Finnish schoolchildren, and South American shamanic ceremonies all instinctively use one specific type of movement - crossing one side of the body over the midline. It turns out to be some of the most neurologically efficient brain training available, and it takes five minutes.

title: The Simple Morning Habit That Protects Your Brain (No Gym Required)
seoTitle: Morning Exercise and Brain Health: A Simple Daily Habit
description: Moving within an hour of waking boosts BDNF, focus, and mood. Learn why morning exercise protects your brain and how to build a 15-minute habit.
author: Lori King, MD
excerpt: One of the strongest predictors of cognitive longevity isn't a supplement or a diet - it's regular movement, and specifically, movement early in the day. Here's why timing matters as much as the activity itself, and how to build the habit without overhauling your morning.

title: The Free "Brain Boost" That's Been Right Outside Your Door
seoTitle: Morning Sunlight and Brain Health: A Free Brain Boost
description: Morning sunlight resets your body clock, lifts mood, sharpens focus, and improves sleep. Here's what early light does for your brain and how to get it.
author: Lori King, MD
excerpt: Pair morning movement with one more free, zero-effort habit and the benefits multiply: morning sunlight. Here's what's actually happening in your brain when early light hits your eyes, and why it's one of the most underrated tools for mood, focus, and sleep.

title: Eat the Rainbow: Why Polyphenols Are Brain Medicine
seoTitle: Polyphenols and Brain Health: Why to Eat the Rainbow
description: Polyphenols fight inflammation, boost blood flow, and help grow new neurons. See the best brain foods, why dark chocolate counts, and the 30-plant goal.
author: Lori King, MD
excerpt: Polyphenols and antioxidants are some of the most powerful brain protectors in nature - and landmark long-term research backs it up. Here's why colorful food matters for cognitive longevity, and yes, why dark chocolate has a legitimate place on the list.
